newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $66, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids were light early Wednesday at $65.00 to $66.00 per cwt and passed by owners pricing cattle at $67.00, steady with the majority of Tuesday's sales, feedlot sources said.
There were reports of light sales late Tuesday at $66.00 but several cattle feeders said the quality of cattle may not have been comparable to those sold at $67.00..
"I'm sure you might be able to find a pen of lower quality that sold at $66.00," a Panhandle area manager said.
Sales Wednesday were expected to be light, following Tuesday's active trading, sources said.
A number of feedyard managers reported selling out their showlists Tuesday at $67.00.
About 55,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 50,000 in Kansas, they said.
"What business there will be will most likely be clean-up," a Kansas feedlot manager said.
Sales also were seen light as the industry starts winding down going into the Memorial Day holiday weekend, with major U.S. meat packers not slaughtering on Monday.
